results.summary_before: This is a demoscene project that displays a bouncing capsule with background and text on a VGA output, accompanied by PDM audio. results.summary_before: This design stores four characters in internal memory and displays them on a 16x4 LED matrix. It accepts four data bits and two position bits to load a hexadecimal character when the load signal is high, and otherwise cycles through the display columns using an internal character map. The design requires an external 16x4 LED matrix connected to the column and line outputs, and it must be reset before use. The documentation is brief but sufficient to understand the basic operation and interface.

results.summary_before: This is version 0.1b of the Basilisc-2816, a small 2-bit serial CPU that executes 8/16-bit instructions and communicates with external memory over a serial interface. It shares the same pinout and architecture as the v0.1a design, using UART pins for memory transactions and debug signals. The design requires an external RP2040 microcontroller, such as on the Tiny Tapeout 7 demo board, to act as a RAM emulator. The documentation for this specific version is minimal, with no test procedure or silicon results provided.

results.summary_before: Oscillating Bones is a ring oscillator built from a chain of 21 SkullFET inverters, producing a square wave output around 90 MHz. It provides divided frequency outputs at 1/2, 1/4, and 1/8 of the base frequency. Silicon tests measured frequencies between 87 and 91 MHz, with some testers observing lower frequencies on divided outputs. It requires an oscilloscope or logic analyzer to observe the output waveforms.
results.summary: Oscillating Bones is a ring oscillator built from a chain of 21 SkullFET inverters, producing a square wave output around 90 MHz. It provides divided frequency outputs at 1/2, 1/4, and 1/8 of the base frequency. Silicon tests measured frequencies between about 87 and 91 MHz on the base and divided outputs, with some testers observing lower frequencies on divided outputs. It requires an oscilloscope or logic analyzer to observe the output waveforms.
